passage: When Pooja got off the tempo at the village school gate, two girls near the well looked at her and giggled. In class, someone passed a note behind her. At recess, Irfan, the boy who sat next to her, finally said quietly, "They're saying your father ran off with the money from the dairy." Pooja's face burned. Her father had gone to the city to work, that was all; he called every night. She wanted to crawl under the desk. Then she wanted to grab the note and tear it up in front of everyone. "Who said it?" she asked, her voice shaking. Irfan shrugged. Pooja sat very still, her fists tight in her lap, not knowing which part of the story to fight first.

qa.q: Where had Pooja's father really gone?
qa.a: Her father had gone to the city to work, and he called every night.

qa.q: What was Pooja feeling after Irfan told her the rumour?
qa.a: She felt shame and anger at once, wanting to crawl under the desk and also to tear up the note, and confused because part of the story was false. 😠

qa.q: What turning point could help Pooja now?
qa.a: She could tell her teacher or her mother what is being said, so an adult can help stop the story instead of her facing it alone.

qa.q: How might Irfan feel after telling Pooja?
qa.a: He may feel awkward and unsure whether he did right, but perhaps also that she deserved to know.

grounding: It shows a girl noticing stares and giggles, learning a partly false story about her family, and feeling shame, anger and confusion.

passage: The bell rang at Dalia's school in Accra, and as she walked to her locker, two boys stopped talking and grinned. A girl near the stairs covered her mouth. At lunch Kofi slid onto the bench beside her. "Dalia, people say you were caught stealing from the corner shop." Dalia stared at him. Last Saturday she had gone back to the shop to return extra change the owner gave her by mistake. Someone must have seen her at the counter with the owner and made up the rest. Her ears went hot. She wanted to run to the toilets and hide. She also wanted to shout at the whole canteen. Instead, she sat frozen, her rice going cold.

qa.q: Why had Dalia gone back to the corner shop?
qa.a: She went back to return extra change the owner gave her by mistake.

qa.q: How can you tell Dalia feels torn between hiding and hitting back?
qa.a: She wanted to run and hide in the toilets and also to shout at the whole canteen, but instead she sat frozen.

qa.q: What would you advise Dalia to do next?
qa.a: Tell a trusted teacher and her family what is being said, and let the shop owner confirm what really happened, rather than facing the rumour alone.

qa.q: What might Kofi be thinking as he watches Dalia freeze?
qa.a: He may be unsure whether the story is true, and worried that telling her made things worse.

grounding: It illustrates a girl who notices stares and learns a partly false story about her, feeling shame and anger and wanting to hide or hit back.
